sources: dossier=Net position 'Uniform terminals' (06-16/17, transcript) established attributes_delta on all three settling terminals, but the later RESOLVED 2026-07-14 parked-state ruling in 'Conflicts needing human ruling' collapses Park's shape to resume_at+scratch+tags, dropping attributes_delta from Park, and 'later intent supersedes earlier' per dossier header; doc=executor.md:28 said every settling terminal carries an attributes delta uniformly; code=executor.proto reserves Park.attributes_delta, callback.go asyncCallbackPark has no AttributesDelta field, corroborating the 07-14 ruling
note: The 06-16/17 uniform-terminals statement was itself superseded by the 07-14 parked-state ruling that strips attributes_delta from Park; doc still reflected the pre-07-14 position. Edited the invariant to say tags are uniform across all three terminals but attributes_delta is Success/Error-only.

sources: dossier=Corrections and restorations record: 'Session-token channel doc drift (2026-07-13, 3f71f90a, finding 56): the token deliberately rides park.scratch; executor.md still said attributes - ruled fix-doc, code is right.' This is a direct, already-adjudicated precedent for this exact row; doc=executor.md:29 said executors carry resume state via attribute carry-forward; code=executor.proto reserves resume_context (field 13) and documents scratch as the park-and-resume carry channel, parked-state.md 'Resume context' section confirms scratch
note: Dossier already ruled this exact finding: code (scratch) is right, doc was stale. Edited the invariant to say resume state rides scratch on Park, not attribute carry-forward.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'Three orthogonal per-node deadlines with 0 = disabled: sync_rpc_deadline (default 30s, ...), max_quiet_period (...), max_runtime (...)' (2026-06-16..17, 055468fc/b31002b8, transcript) states sync_rpc_deadline is per-node, same layer as the other two; doc=executor.md:32 called it an 'executor-template-level' deadline, contrasted against the next invariant's 'per-node' framing; code=template.go SyncRPCDeadline field on TemplateNodeDef, dispatch_deadlines.go resolveSyncRPCDeadline(node, deploymentDefault) corroborates
note: Dossier explicitly enumerates sync_rpc_deadline as one of three orthogonal per-node deadlines, not an executor/template-level declaration. Doc's contrast with the next per-node invariant was false. Fixed to 'per-node'.

sources: dossier=Net position 'Tags, not named events' and Required behaviors line 38: 'registration rejects subscriptions referencing tags outside the emitter's declared_tags; the supervisor's terminal handler rejects settling outcomes carrying undeclared tags (executor protocol-violation error) - the runtime gate was explicitly ratified as a plan step so it would not be silently dropped' (2026-06-16, 055468fc, transcript); doc=executor.md:34 said templates validate emitted tag sets against the advertisement at registration; code=template_validator.go warns (not rejects) on subscription-referenced tags, runner_dispatch.go validateTags rejects undeclared emitted tags at terminal time as executor_protocol_violation, corroborating which object is checked where
note: Doc conflated two different gates: registration checks subscription-referenced tags (dossier states this should reject); emitted-tag enforcement is a terminal-time gate explicitly ratified in the coherence rewrite so it would not be silently dropped. Doc omitted the load-bearing terminal-time gate entirely and misattributed emitted-tag checking to registration. Fixed per dossier's stated split; deferred the warn-vs-reject strength question on the subscription side to a separate code-drift concern outside this row's scope.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific claim (no explicit transcript statement that the handshake is/isn't identical in-proc); design-corpus=decisions/bundled-executor-inproc-capability-advertisement.md states 'the bundled registration entrypoint populates the discovery cache with these at registration time, bypassing the gRPC observability handshake' and 'in-proc handlers receive no gRPC handshake'; doc=executor.md:11 said the observability handshake is identical across both forms; code=inproc_handler.go InProcessHandler exposes only Execute, no observability method, corroborating the decision doc
note: Decision doc and code independently corroborate that in-process handlers never receive the gRPC handshake at all (advertised content is equivalent by construction, but the handshake itself is absent). Two independent artifacts corroborating each other is sufficient provenance per the adjudication model even without a direct dossier statement. Edited the doc to distinguish the outcome vocabulary (identical) from the handshake mechanism (present out-of-process only, bypassed in-process).

sources: dossier=Net position 'In-process executors': 'an inproc transport in the ClientPool switch, explicit registry constructed at startup - no init()-time self-registration' (2026-06-14..18, 752fe200/8e7e4c10, transcript) confirms the mechanism is a registry, not a pool; doc=executor.md:11 said 'dispatch pool'; code=rg for 'dispatch pool|DispatchPool' across lib/, cmd/, test/ returns zero hits, only executor.InProcessRegistry exists
note: Dossier's own vocabulary calls the mechanism a registry; 'dispatch pool' is an undefined term with zero code or design-corpus grounding. Fixed in the same edit as row 277 (same sentence) to 'an in-process handler registry', kept generic prose per the concept-doc self-containment rule (no code symbol citation).

sources: dossier=Net position 'Scratch': 'Scratch carries byte-for-byte across in-place retry, stale_recovery, and recalculate' (2026-06-14..22, 752fe200/10cf843b, transcript) explicitly lists cascade-driven recalculate alongside the two recovery paths as a scratch-carrying disposition; doc=executor.md:19 said scratch carries forward only via recovery enqueue paths, not via normal cascade re-fires; code=cascade_recalculate.go loads prior row's scratch (LoadScratchInTx) and enqueues with PriorDispatchDisposition recalculate, corroborating the dossier
note: Dossier explicitly names recalculate (the cascade-driven enqueue) as a scratch-carrying disposition alongside retry and stale_recovery, directly contradicting the doc's 'not via normal cascade re-fires' claim. Reworded the invariant around the real boundary: any dispatch that supersedes a prior one carries scratch forward; a fresh dispatch with no predecessor does not.

sources: dossier=silent on concept-catalog partition between executor and observability (dossier addresses executor behavior, not doc-organization boundaries); doc=executor.md:23 Boundaries 'Owns: ... the observability protocol surface' vs observability.md:19 Boundaries 'Owns: the optional service protocols, the handshake mechanism, the refresh-loop policy...', both list the other as adjacent
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): observability.md is the sole owner of the service-observability protocol surface (handshake, capability advertisement mechanics, refresh-loop policy) — the surface is deliberately uniform across service kinds and must not be sliced per-service. executor.md's Owns entry moved to Does-NOT-own with a cross-reference; it describes only what the executor advertises through the surface.
